title: EleutherIA: An AI-Powered Scholarly Research Platform for Ancient Philosophy on Free Will
description: EleutherIA is an open scholarly research platform and FAIR-aligned knowledge graph for ancient debates on free will, fate, moral responsibility, and agency across the Greco-Roman and early Christian worlds. This archive combines a curated knowledge graph, an ancient-text corpus, and an agentic GraphRAG stack for citation-grounded question answering, graph exploration, and data quality auditing. As of the 2026-03-10 audit bundled with this release, the live graph contains 17,396 nodes, 42,161 edges, and 13,293 passage citations; the broader platform indexes 189 ancient works and more than 16,500 passages in Greek, Latin, and English. Coverage spans roughly twelve centuries, from the Presocratics and Classical Greek philosophy through Hellenistic, Roman Imperial, Patristic, and Late Antique authors, while also linking ancient primary sources to modern scholarship and reception history. The repository includes the application code, database migrations, ingestion and repair scripts, evaluation reports, and documentation needed to reproduce, inspect, and extend the archive.
